name: Halloween Horror Nights
summary: An adult horror event rather than a Halloween party. For the remaining 2026 run, compare available weeknights first; a busy October Saturday without event Express Pass can leave little time for all ten houses.
h1: Halloween Horror Nights Orlando: what the ticket buys, which nights to pick, and who should not go
title: Halloween Horror Nights Orlando
description: Universal Studios Florida's 2026 hard-ticket horror event: confirmed dates and houses, the labelled 2025 price band, which nights to buy, and who should not go.

typicalWindow.hours: Roughly 18:30 to 01:00 on most nights and later on peak weekend dates, with the park closing to daytime guests in the late afternoon and reopening as a ticketed event

pricing.cheapestNights: Wednesday and Thursday nights in the first two weeks of the run
pricing.priciestNights: Fridays and Saturdays in the second half of October, and Halloween night itself
notes: Tax is additional, and Universal prices every night separately. The gap between a quiet early-run weeknight and a peak October Saturday has been larger than the cheapest ticket costs.

Multi-night passes change the arithmetic completely. Universal has sold blocks-of-nights passes for several seasons, and two visits on one of those has usually cost less than two single-night tickets.
Express Pass for this event is a separate product from the daytime Express Pass, priced by date, and on peak October dates it has cost more than the event ticket itself.
The Express Pass included with a stay at Universal's premier hotels does not cover this event. That is the most expensive wrong assumption a first-time visitor makes here.
Annual Passholder pricing has appeared on some dates in past seasons and is worth checking before you buy, but it has not reached the peak October weekends.

whatYouGet: Around ten walk-through haunted houses, built inside soundstages and purpose-built tents and staffed by several hundred performers. This is the product, and nothing else at an American theme park is doing it at this scale.

Four new scare zones filling the streets between the houses in 2026, plus other street experiences. These are free-roaming rather than queued, which makes them the part of the event you cannot avoid once you are inside.
Two live shows in 2026 — Stranger Things: Return to Hawkins and Nightmare Fuel: Blood Noir — plus event-only food and drink offerings.
A short list of the park's regular rides operating during event hours, weighted toward the headliners rather than the family attractions.
The Tribute Store, a retail build-out in the New York area themed as heavily as the houses, which is free to walk through and takes about ten minutes.

An early-house option if you also have same-day daytime admission, or buy the separate Scream Early add-on with your event ticket. For 2026 Universal advertises Scream Early entry after 2 p.m. and access to at least three houses; check its current entry rules before buying.
whatYouDont: A family event. Universal's own guidance is that this is not recommended for anyone under thirteen, and it means it. There is no age limit at the gate and no ID check, so the decision sits entirely with the adult buying the ticket.

A costume night on a standard HHN ticket. Universal prohibits guest costumes and costume masks on regular event nights. Its separate 2026 Premium Scream Night product has a costume exception subject to detailed rules, so check the exact ticket and policy before dressing for the event.
Short queues. On a peak October Saturday the marquee houses have run past 90 minutes each, and a night without Express Pass realistically gets you four or five of the ten.
The full daytime park. Most family attractions do not operate during event hours; check the current event map or Universal app for the participating ride list.
Any coverage from your hotel's Express Pass. The Express Unlimited included at the premier hotels is a daytime benefit and admits you to nothing during the event.
A refund or a rain check. The event runs in rain. The houses stay open because they are indoors; the scare zones, the show, and the outdoor queues are what suffer.

A guaranteed house lineup when tickets first go on sale. Universal announces houses in stages across the summer, so an early purchase may be made before the full list is public. All ten 2026 houses are now confirmed in the edition below.

verdict.short: For the remaining 2026 run, compare available weeknights first and price event Express Pass if a peak October date is your only option. This is genuinely not for young children.
worthItIf: You actually like horror. This is a gore, fog, and jump-scare event for its full length, and liking Halloween is not the same thing as liking this.
You can travel on a remaining Wednesday or Thursday and compare its actual ticket price with the weekend dates available to you.
You will buy Express Pass or a multi-night pass if your only dates fall in October. Both cost real money, and both cost less than paying peak price for a night in which you see four houses.
Your group is adults or older teenagers who have each opted in, rather than one enthusiast and three people who were brought along.
You can arrive before the event opens, or qualify for Universal's 2026 early-house access and use the extra time for houses that matter most to your group.
skipIf: Anyone in your group is under about thirteen. Universal will not stop you at the gate, and that is not the same as the event being suitable.

Anyone in your group is pregnant, has a heart condition, or is strongly affected by strobe lighting. The houses run heavy fog, sustained strobes, and loud sudden noise for their entire length, and there is no quieter route through them.
You want to ride. The operating list during event hours is short and the queues are long. A normal park day costs less and delivers several times the rides.
Your only available date is an October Saturday and you will not buy Express Pass. That combination is the most common way people spend event money on a night they do not enjoy.
You were hoping to do the daytime park and the event on one ticket. They are two separate purchases, and the event on its own is a full evening that ends after midnight.

strategy.heading: Pick the night before you pick anything else
body: The date decides your night more than any other choice you make here. Early-run midweek dates have historically paired lower ticket prices with shorter queues, but those 2026 dates have passed; compare the remaining nights in Universal's live ticket calendar before committing.

October weekends are the opposite on both counts. The marquee houses run past 90 minutes, the walkways between them clog to a shuffle, and the event sells out. If that is your only window, budget for Express Pass rather than hoping the crowd is light.

Halloween night may be among the dearest and busiest dates, but price and availability change. If a remaining weeknight works for your trip, compare its current price and expected queue trade-off before paying a Halloween premium.

Sunday is the underrated night in the back half of the run. It prices below Friday and Saturday, it draws a smaller local crowd than either, and it is the only weekend date that still behaves like a weeknight.

strategy.heading: Express Pass, and the arithmetic that decides it
body: Budget for event Express Pass on a peak October weekend if doing most houses in one night is the goal. On a lower-demand weeknight, compare its live date-specific price with the cost of an additional event night before buying.

Universal sells a separate Express Pass for this event, priced by date in the same way the ticket is. The standard version covers one express entry per house rather than unlimited re-entry, which is a distinction people discover at the second house rather than at the point of sale.

The Express Unlimited included with a stay at Universal's premier hotels is a daytime product. It does not admit you to a single house on an event night. Guests who booked those hotels specifically for this and found out at the first queue are a fixture of every season.

The comparison worth running is not Express Pass against nothing. It is one October Saturday with Express Pass against two early-run weeknights on a multi-night pass. On most seasons the two weeknights win on houses seen per dollar, and it is not close.

strategy.heading: Working the houses
body: Start at the far end of the park and work back toward the entrance. Most of the crowd attacks the first house it sees, which stacks the longest queues nearest the gate for the opening hour and leaves the far sites comparatively open.

The houses sit in two clusters: the soundstages toward the front of the park, and the tented sites reached through the far end. The tents are the longer walk, which is exactly why they are the ones to do first.

The final hour is the second-best hour of the night. Queues at the back of the park fall away once the day-trip crowd starts leaving, and the last 45 minutes routinely buys two houses that cost 90 minutes each earlier in the evening.

Do not repeat a house until you have done all ten, and do not queue for food between about nine and eleven. Ten houses is more than most people manage once; repeats and a 40-minute food line are what turn eight houses into five.

strategy.heading: What an event night does to the rest of your trip
body: An event night replaces the evening of a park day rather than extending one. Universal Studios Florida closes to daytime guests in the late afternoon and reopens as a ticketed event, so a day ticket does not admit you in and an event ticket does not admit you before the changeover.

The 2026 early-access rules deserve a fresh look: Universal advertises a Scream Early add-on that admits same-day HHN ticket holders to Universal Studios Florida after 2 p.m., with access to at least three houses, provided they enter by 5 p.m. Guests who already hold daytime park admission should verify the current Stay & Scream procedure rather than relying on an older holding-area plan.
Write off the following morning. The event runs past one in the morning on most nights and later on peak weekends, and early entry at the parks is at the other end of the same clock.

Islands of Adventure and Epic Universe run normal hours on event nights, which makes the afternoon before an event night the right time to be at either of them rather than at the park that is about to close around you.

strategy.heading: Who should not be there, and why we say it plainly
body: Universal advises against attendance for children under thirteen and does not enforce an age limit. Both halves of that sentence matter: the advice is serious, and nothing at the turnstile will act on it for you.

The content is sustained rather than occasional. Each house is several minutes of low light, dense fog, strobes, loud sudden noise, and performers who move toward you and follow you out. The scare zones do the same thing outdoors, with no queue to step out of and no way to route around them once you are inside the park.
There is no toned-down version of a house and no marked quiet path through the event. The only accommodation available is not going in.

If you are in Orlando with young children and want a Halloween evening, this is the wrong event and there is no daytime children's version of it here to fall back on. Plan that evening somewhere else rather than assuming the first hour will be gentle.

faqs.q: Is Halloween Horror Nights suitable for children?
faqs.a: No, and Universal says so. Its published guidance is that the event is not recommended for anyone under thirteen. There is no age limit at the gate and no ID check, so the decision sits with the adult buying the ticket. This is not a Halloween overlay with a few scares in it: each house is several minutes of strobes, fog, gore, and performers who follow guests, and there is no gentler route through the event.

faqs.q: Do I need a separate ticket, or does my park ticket work?
faqs.a: Separate, in both directions. Universal Studios Florida closes to daytime guests in the late afternoon and reopens as a ticketed event, so a day ticket does not admit you to the event and an event ticket does not admit you during the day. If you want both halves of that day you are buying both tickets, and the combination makes for a very long day that ends after midnight.

faqs.q: Does the Express Pass included with my hotel work at the event?
faqs.a: No. Universal Express Unlimited included with a stay at the premier hotels is a daytime benefit and covers nothing during event hours. Event Express Pass is a separate purchase, priced by date like the ticket, and it sells out on peak nights. This is the most expensive assumption people make about this event, and it is made at the first house queue rather than before booking.

faqs.q: How many houses can I actually do in one night?
faqs.a: Four or five without Express Pass on a busy October night, and eight to ten on a quiet early-run weeknight if you start at the far end of the park and do not repeat anything. That range is the entire argument for choosing an early weeknight: the ticket costs less and delivers roughly twice the content for the same hours on your feet.

Not on a standard Halloween Horror Nights night: Universal prohibits guest costumes and costume masks. The separate 2026 Premium Scream Night product has a costume exception under Universal's detailed costume policy; the remaining Premium Scream Night is October 19. Check the operator's current rules for permitted attire and face paint before buying or dressing for that date.

faqs.q: Are the house lineups announced before tickets go on sale?
faqs.a: Not all of them. Universal sold 2026 tickets before the full house lineup was public and announced houses in stages. All ten 2026 houses are now confirmed on Universal's official haunted-houses page and listed in the 2026 edition below.

It is most useful when your only 2026 date is a busy October weekend and you want to see most of the houses in one night. Event Express Pass is a separate date-priced purchase and provides one Express entry at each house. Compare its current price with another available event night or a multi-night pass before buying.

Yes. Universal's August 28 opening announcement confirms 49 select event nights through November 1, 2026 at Universal Studios Florida, and has published all ten house names. A start-to-end window does not mean the event runs every night; check Universal's ticket calendar for the specific night and current price before booking.

changes: The run again extended past forty nights, continuing more than a decade of the event growing at both ends of its calendar.
Around ten houses ran, split between licensed horror properties and originals created for the event, which has been the standing shape for several seasons.
Per-night pricing continued to spread, with the cheapest early-run weeknights sitting at well under half the peak October Saturday rate before tax.

freshness.sourceNote: 2025 season figures, stated as 2025 figures: select nights at Universal Studios Florida from late August to the first weekend of November, around ten houses, and a per-night ticket band of roughly $75 to $185 before tax. We have not re-verified the final night count or the house list for that season, so neither is published as precise here, and the price band is stated as a band rather than as a quote.
